Someone throws Adam into a dark shaft, and he falls.

flagged.title: Acts 3-4: Escalation & the Ending
flagged.reason: The video repeats multiple mark-affecting errors regarding character endings and plot events: stating Danny is medicated instead of Brian, misattributing Leah's line 'What are you thinking?' to Richard, claiming Phil sits eating in silence, asserting Cathy enters television in the Act 4 aftermath rather than leading the gang violently, and stating Leah's disappearance has no explanation.

mark_affecting.quote: Danny and several others are now relying on medication just to cope with severe anxiety and depression.
And Richard just sits with Phil, trying to spark conversation, asking 'what are you thinking?'
now sits completely alone in a field, eating in silence, just staring blankly into space.
And Cathy, the one who showed zero remorse? Yeah, she's moved into a successful television career.
In Act 4, Leah simply vanishes. Kelly gives us absolutely no explanation.

Kelly strongly implies that Phil orders the group to kill Adam. But, and this is key, he never explicitly spells out the exact instructions. By leaving this deliberately ambiguous, Kelly forces us, the audience, to infer what happens based purely on the characters' reactions.

flagged.title: Character Analysis
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly claims that we never hear Adam's perspective and that he is kept silent, when in Act 3 he speaks at length, and it incorrectly attributes being medicated to Danny rather than Brian.

mark_affecting.quote: Adam barely appears. We never hear his perspective. He is kept silent and almost totally invisible to us.

mark_affecting.video_says: Take Danny. Poor Danny just wanted to be a dentist, but he becomes increasingly anxious and eventually ends up on medication.
mark_affecting.lesson_says: Brian is the clearest example of the cost: he cries throughout, is forced to lie to the police, and by Act 4 he is on stronger and stronger medication and may be sectioned. Danny’s plan to be a dentist ends in work experience he hates.
